scams.name: Tenerife South (TFS) / Tenerife North (TFN) Airport Taxi Overcharge
scams.description: Tenerife's two airports serve different purposes: TFS (south) handles the bulk of package-tourism traffic, while TFN (north) serves inter-island and domestic flights. Both have documented taxi-overcharge patterns. Legitimate licensed taxi fares from TFS: Playa de las Américas €25–€30, Los Cristianos €18–€22, Santa Cruz €45–€55. From TFN: Santa Cruz €18–€22, Puerto de la Cruz €25–€30. r/Tenerife 'Question about taxis and receiving change?' (comments/vfxjdz) gives the local view: 'Taxi prices are indeed intransparent (in almost every country)' — the local concern is less about outright overcharging than about intransparent fare calculations. r/GoingToSpain 'Beware of this taxi scam' (comments/1mk8n4c, 2025) documents the Spain-wide blurry-meter pattern that applies in Tenerife as well. The package-tourism context is relevant: many UK/Irish visitors have pre-booked transfers through their tour operator (TUI, Jet2, easyJet Holidays) — these are usually honest, but the 'oh wait my transfer didn't arrive, can you drive me?' opportunist-taxi variant at arrival exits is documented. For older travelers arriving on package holidays, the practical playbook: (1) if pre-booked transfer is included, wait at the designated meeting point — do NOT engage with drivers who approach unsolicited; (2) for independent taxi, use the licensed rank outside arrivals and insist on the meter; (3) confirm approximate fare before boarding (€25–€30 to Playa de las Américas from TFS); (4) Cabify operates on Tenerife with app-regulated fares; (5) TITSA public buses serve most resort destinations at €3–€10 but are package-luggage-unfriendly.
scams.avoidance: If pre-booked transfer is included, wait at the designated tour-operator meeting point For independent taxi, use licensed rank outside arrivals and insist on the meter Confirm approximate fare: €25–€30 TFS to Playa de las Américas, €18–€22 Los Cristianos, €45–€55 Santa Cruz Cabify operates on Tenerife with app-regulated fares — use for predictable pricing Photograph taxi plate number from rear windscreen on entering
scams.location: Tenerife Sur Reina Sofía Airport (TFS), Tenerife Norte Los Rodeos Airport (TFN), Playa de las Américas and Los Cristianos return-ride pickups

scams.name: Playa de las Américas Pickpockets & Robberies
scams.description: Playa de las Américas has the Canary Islands' most-documented street-crime problem. r/Tenerife 'Robbed in Las Americas, real' (comments/1888q1z, 2024) is a named anchor documenting an armed robbery: 'In Las Americas? Not common with a gun, but robberies, muggings and pickpocketing is an ever growi' ng concern, particularly on the Veronicas nightlife strip and in side streets leading away from the main promenade. r/Tenerife 'Is thievery a problem in Tenerife?' (comments/xe6ut1) gives the baseline: 'Most crime is opportunistic. Tourists get very complacent. At any tourist-heavy location, lock your' valuables and stay aware. The Las Américas-specific risk zones: (1) Veronicas nightlife strip side-street exits during 2–5 AM return windows; (2) Playa del Camisón and Playa de las Vistas beach crowds during summer afternoons; (3) Calle Noelia Afonso Cabrera shopping strip; (4) Safari shopping centre and hotel lobbies during evening peak. The scam patterns: opportunistic phone snatch during outdoor-dining conversations, wallet lifts during nightclub dance-floor crush, bag theft from beach towels, and the occasional armed mugging of tourists walking drunk late at night. For older travelers on a package holiday, the practical defence: (1) crossbody bag zipped in front during any Las Américas walking; (2) leave passport, backup card, and excess cash in the resort safe; carry only €20–€40 and one card for an evening; (3) avoid walking alone between the Veronicas strip and your hotel after 2 AM — use the resort's taxi-desk pre-booking; (4) at beach, rent a chiringuito locker or leave valuables in the resort; (5) file denuncia at Policía Local Arona (Playa de las Américas, +34 922 757 610) within 48 hours for insurance.
scams.avoidance: Wear zipped crossbody bag in front during any Las Américas walking Carry only €20–€40 and one card for an evening; passport + backup in resort safe Never walk alone between Veronicas and hotel after 2 AM — use resort taxi-desk pre-booking Beach: rent chiringuito locker or leave valuables in resort File denuncia at Policía Local Arona (+34 922 757 610) within 48 hours for insurance
scams.location: Playa de las Américas nightlife strip (Calle Noelia Afonso Cabrera), Los Cristianos beachfront, Veronicas strip bars, Costa Adeje shopping centres

scams.name: Tenerife Rental Car Scams — Europcar Tenerife Sur Flagged
scams.description: Tenerife's rental-car scam pattern mirrors Bilbao and Málaga, but with a specific 2025 named anchor for Europcar at TFS. r/GoingToSpain 'Beware of latest rental car scam in Spain' (comments/1ei4kan, 2025) contains a French-language comment flagging Europcar TFS directly: 'A tenerife (aéroport sud), j'ai essayé EUROPCAR, quelle erreur!' — meaning a rental-customer specifically warns about Europcar at Tenerife Sur airport. r/VisitingTenerife 'Car Rental Scams' (comments/1qscrkn, 2025) is a 2025 named-anchor community thread discussing recent victim accounts including 'Car Rental Deposit SCAM (Not Refun' ded) where deposits were retained after return. r/askspain 'Help needed: car rental scam, what can I do?' (comments/1l4ah45, 2025) adds the 2025 victim-remedy framing: 'this company clearly has a unusually high rat' e of complaints and chargeback disputes are the practical remedy. The broader pattern matches Spain-wide: (1) post-return damage claims with fabricated photos; (2) mandatory CDW upsells at 2–3x online rate; (3) deposit retention after return citing 'late return' or 'cleaning fees'; (4) fuel-policy 'return empty' overcharging. For older travelers on a Tenerife package holiday, the protective playbook: (1) AVOID Europcar at TFS, Goldcar, Centauro, OK Mobility — community-flagged; (2) book direct with Cicar (Canary-Islands-based, high community trust) or Hertz for better reliability; (3) at pickup, video a walk-around narrating visible marks; (4) photograph all sides, roof, wheels, and undercarriage via phone camera through wheel well; (5) decline CDW upsells if your credit card provides car-rental insurance; (6) on return, video the vehicle and retain the fuel receipt; (7) dispute damage claims with your credit card within 48 hours using your evidence.
scams.avoidance: AVOID Europcar TFS, Goldcar, Centauro, OK Mobility — community-flagged repeat offenders Book direct with Cicar (Canary-Islands-based) or Hertz for better reliability Video walk-around narrating visible marks at pickup before signing paperwork Photograph all sides, roof, wheels, undercarriage via phone camera through wheel well Dispute damage claims with credit card within 48 hours using photo/video evidence
scams.location: TFS airport rental desks (Europcar specifically flagged, Goldcar, Centauro, OK Mobility), city-centre rental offices, resort-strip operators

scams.name: Tenerife Timeshare Pressure Sales — £28m UK Elder-Fraud Network
scams.description: Tenerife has Europe's most-documented timeshare-fraud ecosystem, specifically targeting older UK travelers. r/TenerifeNews 'Tenerife links to monster £28m UK timeshare scam that' (comments/1oa9jvn, 2025) is a named 2025 police-investigation anchor: a £28 million UK timeshare scam 'that targeted elderly' victims originating from Canary Islands operations. The scam pattern has been refined over decades: OPC ('off-property contact') reps approach tourists on the street with 'free scratchcards' that always 'win' a prize; the prize requires attending a 90-minute 'presentation'; the presentation uses high-pressure closing tactics, psychological manipulation, and binding contracts signed under duress that leave victims committed to €10,000–€50,000+ timeshare obligations. r/TimeshareOwners 'PLS READ and don't ban: Spanish timeshare contracts can' (comments/1mumgdg, 2025) documents the 2025 legal-remedy landscape: 'Spanish timeshare contracts' signed after 1999 under the Spanish Timeshare Act can be legally voided if certain disclosure requirements were not met, but victims must act within statutory deadlines. r/AskUK 'Do you know anyone who ever had a timeshare?' (comments/1lcnqk1, 2025) captures the UK-victim reality: 'They are not scams since you do actually get a product you can use for the money you spend' — technically true but the sales tactics and contract bindings are the scam genre. For older UK, Irish, and Northern European travelers on a Tenerife holiday, the protective playbook: (1) NEVER accept a 'free scratchcard' from a street tout in Playa de las Américas, Los Cristianos, or Costa Adeje; (2) decline all invitations to 'presentations,' 'holiday-club meetings,' or 'resort tours' — these are timeshare-closing venues; (3) if you've attended a presentation and signed anything, use Spain's 14-day cooling-off period (Ley 4/2012) to rescind — contact a Spanish timeshare solicitor (timeshare-consumer.org) within that window; (4) do not pay any 'deposit' or 'activation fee' at the venue; (5) if you suspect the £28m UK scam network per r/TenerifeNews, contact UK Action Fraud and Spanish Guardia Civil (+34 062).
scams.avoidance: NEVER accept 'free scratchcards' from street touts in Canary Islands resort strips Decline all invitations to 'presentations,' 'holiday-club meetings,' or 'resort tours' If you've signed anything, use Spain's 14-day cooling-off period to rescind (Ley 4/2012) Do not pay any deposit or 'activation fee' at the presentation venue Report suspected fraud to UK Action Fraud and Spanish Guardia Civil (+34 062)
scams.location: Timeshare presentation venues in Playa de las Américas, Los Cristianos, Costa Adeje; 'scratchcard' street touts pushing tourists toward presentation rooms; OPC (off-property contact) reps

scams.name: Teide National Park Permit & Tour Package Scams
scams.description: Mount Teide is Tenerife's #1 natural attraction — Spain's highest peak at 3,718 m — and the summit-access permit system has generated a specific scam ecosystem. r/VisitingTenerife 'A bit confused on Teide permit - Opinions on volcanoteide' (comments/1o16l6w, 2025) is a named 2025 community thread: 'we decided to visit Tenerife on a short time and as a surprise to no one, all the permits to' summit Teide are already sold out — permits must be booked months ahead at reservasparquesnacionales.es (the official Parques Nacionales booking system). The scam: third-party operators (volcanoteide.com is one mentioned in community threads, though its legitimacy is debated) sell 'skip-the-queue' summit tours at €80–€150 per person, bundling the permit with an unnecessary guide. r/Tenerife 'The Güimar pyramids are the worst tourist trap' (comments/1j04f29, 2025) is a named 2025 community PSA about a related tourist-trap venue: the 'Güimar Pyramids,' marketed as ancient stepped pyramids, are actually 19th-century agricultural terraces with no archaeological significance — a €17 entry fee for a minor historical curiosity wrapped in pseudo-archaeological marketing. r/CanaryIslands 'We are unsure if Playa de las Americas fits ou requirements' (comments/1dk2as6, 2024) gives the broader tourist-trap framing for Tenerife excursion packages: 'traps in terms of bars' and tours. For older travelers on a Tenerife holiday who want to visit Teide, the practical alternatives: (1) the Mount Teide cable car to the 3,555 m station is €45.50 adult (free summit permit NOT required for cable-car-to-viewpoint only, only for final 200 m summit hike); (2) book cable car direct at volcanoteide.com (this IS the official Teleférico del Teide site); (3) the €10 Teide National Park entry is FREE (there is no general park entry fee); (4) for the summit-permit hike, book 3+ months ahead at reservasparquesnacionales.es (free); (5) skip hotel-concierge 'Teide excursion' packages at €80–€150 — a self-guided rental-car + cable-car visit costs €45 per person; (6) skip Güimar Pyramids and La Laguna 'tourist traps' per 2025 community PSAs.
scams.avoidance: Book Teide cable car direct at volcanoteide.com — €45.50 adult; visit the 3,555 m viewpoint station For summit-permit hike, book 3+ months ahead at reservasparquesnacionales.es (free) Teide National Park general entry is FREE — reject any 'ecological fee' claims Skip hotel-concierge 'Teide excursion' packages — self-guided rental-car + cable-car is €45 per person Skip Güimar Pyramids and similar 'tourist-trap' attractions per r/Tenerife 2025 PSA
scams.location: Teide National Park visitor centre, Mount Teide cable car queue, hotel-concierge 'Teide excursion' bookings, tout stalls in Playa de las Américas

scams.name: Tenerife Airbnb, Camper Van & Short-Term Rental Fraud
scams.description: Tenerife's rental-accommodation scam has a specific 2025 named-anchor variant covering camper-van rentals. r/GoingToSpain 'Tenerife Airbnb Scam' (comments/1rbvf8i, 2025) is a named 2025 first-person account: 'Rented camper van off Airbnb to drive which was returned in perfect condition. Paid €400 on Pa' yPal — the victim later received a fabricated damage claim after returning the camper van in perfect condition. The scam pattern exploits Airbnb's expansion into vehicle rentals and unusual experiences; the host sent a PayPal invoice post-return claiming damages the victim had photos disproving. r/Tenerife 'is it an scam? A friend who is traveling on Tenerife got' (comments/14nhj8k, 2024) documents an older variant of the bracelet/friendship-item scam: 'It's a common tactic, they tie to your wrists and say it's free hoping you'd feel bad and give some' thing in return. r/Scams 'Scams in real life - this is a pretty good guide' (comments/pij1bp, 2024) includes Tenerife cross-references. The broader Tenerife rental-fraud pattern matches Spain-wide: (1) listing 20–30% below comparable platform-verified rates; (2) off-platform payment requests (PayPal, Bizum, bank transfer); (3) double-booked listings; (4) post-return fabricated damage claims. For older travelers considering Tenerife accommodation longer than a package-holiday week, the protective playbook: (1) book only through Airbnb, Booking.com, or VRBO with platform-verified payment and cancellation protection; (2) for Airbnb Experiences or vehicle rentals, take photo/video evidence at pickup AND return; (3) refuse PayPal, Bizum, Western Union, or cryptocurrency payments for deposits or damage claims — all legitimate disputes go through platform channels; (4) verify the property's Canary Islands VV (Vivienda Vacacional) tourist registration number — required for all licensed short-term rentals; (5) if defrauded, file a denuncia at Policía Nacional Tenerife (Santa Cruz: Ramón y Cajal 2, +34 922 849 500) and dispute via credit card chargeback within 48 hours.
scams.avoidance: Book only through Airbnb, Booking.com, or VRBO with platform-verified payment For Airbnb Experiences or vehicle rentals, take photo/video evidence at pickup AND return Refuse PayPal, Bizum, Western Union, or cryptocurrency payments for deposits or damages Verify the Canary Islands VV tourist-registration number on the listing File denuncia at Policía Nacional Tenerife (+34 922 849 500) and credit card chargeback within 48 hours
scams.location: Airbnb Tenerife listings, camper-van hire platforms, private referral 'holiday villa' agencies, Paypal-invoice scam variants
